text: Level sets: moving interfaces and comparison with VOF A level set embeds a curve or surface as the zero contour of a grid function and evolves that function. It connects transport, Hamilton–Jacobi equations and interface geometry, with a representation that naturally accommodates merging and splitting. Start with the equations, then inspect small reproducible two-dimensional circle motions. Function values are neither fluid density nor volume fraction. A monotone transformation retaining the zero set leaves the interface unchanged while changing gradients and numerical behavior. Some sources reverse the sign; normals and normal speeds must use the same convention. Geometric area clips linear phi on triangles and compares against pi*r², retaining initial geometric bias. Coupled grid/time refinement of advection alone observes about1.90 for translation and2.02 for rotation. SeparateN64 CFL-halving sensitivity is recorded; this is not a proof of pure spatial order. Finest-grid worst relative area error changes about0.22% to0.93% for translation and1.06% to2.02% for rotation, from advection alone to redistancing. The simple redistancing increases error in these fixed runs. Distance-gradient quality, zero-interface accuracy and enclosed-volume balance are distinct diagnostics. Scope and related reading This release transports circles in prescribed velocities. It does not validate topology changes, curvature flow, surface tension or two-phase flow, nor benchmark VOF performance. Downloads retain analytic reference formulas, full2D final fields, intermediate interface samples, CSV, input hashes, all decisions and each redistancing area change. The existing Zalesak slotted-disk material is a separate conservative scalar-transport example; its code is not relabeled as a VOF implementation.
